findings.title: Data race on counter and loop variable in concurrent index init
findings.body: In searchSupport.init the for _, info := range stats loop launches group.Go(func() error { ... info ...; totalBatchesIndexed++ ... }) with concurrency up to initWorkers. totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int incremented from multiple goroutines with no atomic/mutex, which is a data race and corrupts the indexed count reported in the span event. The closure also captures the loop variable info; on Go versions before per-iteration scoping this builds the wrong namespace/group/resource concurrently. Fix by copying info into a loop-local variable and using an atomic counter.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock causing data race
findings.body: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache directly with no b.cacheMu.RLock, while BuildIndex now inserts into b.cache under b.cacheMu.Lock concurrently and GetIndex reads under RLock. Concurrent map read+write is a fatal data race/panic in Go. The finer-grain locking in BuildIndex made this reachable during parallel startup builds. Fix by holding RLock around the iteration and DocCount collection.

findings.title: History/Origin panic when search is not configured
findings.body: Server.History calls s.search.History and Server.Origin calls s.search.Origin with no nil check, while Server.Search does check s.search == nil. When the server is constructed without Search.Resources, s.search is nil, so any History or Origin RPC dereferences a nil pointer and panics the gRPC server instead of returning an error. Add the same not-configured guard as Search.

findings.title: Search watch goroutine leaks and busy-loops on closed channel
findings.body: searchSupport.init creates watchctx := context.Background() with no cancel and loops with v := <-events calling s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) without checking ok. The channel returned by WatchWriteEvents is closed on backend shutdown, at which point the receive returns the zero value immediately forever, causing a hot infinite loop indexing nil events, and the poller tied to the discarded context can never be stopped. Fix by deriving watchctx from the server lifecycle context with cancel and breaking on !ok.

findings.title: No per-key guard allows duplicate concurrent BuildIndex for same key
findings.body: The change removed the global cacheMu lock around the whole BuildIndex and now only locks around the final b.cache[key] = idx assignment. Two concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. from init workers plus getOrCreateIndex on a concurrent Search) will both create a bleve index, run the builder, and overwrite each other. For file-backed indexes bleve.New on the same directory will fail or lock, turning a duplicate-build inefficiency into user-visible Search errors. Fix with per-key singleflight/mutex so only one build per key runs at a time.
